strengths: Well-motivated problem: Clearly identifies gap in existing work (visual-centric vs. audio-centric control) and proposes unified multi-modal framework for joint audio-video generation

Comprehensive experimental evaluation: Multiple quantitative metrics (Sync-C/D, Text CLIP, Subject DINO), human evaluation with 20 participants across 6 criteria, qualitative comparisons across control modalities
Practical architecture design: MMCU provides elegant unified interface for heterogeneous inputs; Dual-Stream Bypass preserves pretrained weights; zero-initialization ensures training stability
Efficient training: 7,200 steps in 12 hours on 4 H200s demonstrates practical scalability without excessive computational requirements
Flexible inference control: Modality-specific guidance scaling (Figure 7) enables intuitive decoupled control over visual identity and audio timbre, with clear ablation showing effect
Audio quality analysis: Appendix B evaluates speaker similarity, naturalness (UTMOS), and transcription accuracy beyond just synchronization metrics
Clear presentation: Well-structured paper with informative architecture diagrams (Figures 2-3), effective qualitative comparisons, and comprehensive results tables
weaknesses: Incremental technical novelty: Bypass architecture adapts ControlNet/T2I-Adapter patterns straightforwardly; MMCU is standard concatenation+masking; guidance scaling is simple multiplicative factor. Strong engineering but limited fundamental innovation

Critical missing ablations: No analysis of MMCU design choices; no study of what bypass branches learn or their individual contributions; no ablation of bypass injection points (why even-numbered layers?); limited guidance scaling analysis (single example)

Severe evaluation scope limitation: All evaluation confined to portrait/talking-head animation (single character). Trained on 30K portrait-only Hallo3 data. No evaluation on diverse scenes, full-body motion, multiple characters, or complex backgrounds. Directly contradicts problem framing as 'joint audio-video generation' which implies broader domain

Strong proprietary model dependency: Entire approach builds on unreleased LTX-2. No ablation showing MMControl's contribution vs. base model capability. Reproducibility severely compromised. Cannot assess how much improvement comes from MMCU/bypass vs. LTX-2 inherent quality

Unfair experimental comparison (Table 1): MMControl jointly generates speech+video (harder); baselines use ground-truth audio+first frame (easier). Different tasks conflated. Sync-D higher for baselines (10.2-10.7 vs 10.5), indicating trade-offs not acknowledged

Underdeveloped audio control: Acoustic MMCU minimal (reference audio + silence placeholders). Paper explicitly states pitch/energy contours are 'future extensions.' No comparison with audio-centric methods (MoCha, Wan2.2-S2V) from related work. Acoustic timbre control underanalyzed

Insufficient structural control analysis: Mean MAE 4.52 shows incremental improvement over VACE (5.35). Only qualitative pose comparisons. No systematic analysis of fine-grained pose detail consistency. Quantitative pose error metrics absent

Statistical rigor gaps: No error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests on quantitative results. Human evaluation modest (20 participants × 5 samples = 100 ratings). No inter-rater agreement (Cohen's κ) reported. Improvements appear small without significance analysis (e.g., 0.2546 vs 0.2337 Text CLIP)

Reproducibility concerns: Depends on proprietary Qwen2.5-Omni for captions; preprocessing uses proprietary tools (Grounded-SAM-2, Depth-Anything-v2, DWPose); no code release mentioned; training details incomplete (warmup schedule, gradient clipping, augmentation specifics)

Limited failure analysis: No discussion of failure modes or edge cases. Single example for decoupled control (Figure 7). Missing analysis: What happens with conflicting conditions (pose vs. text)? How does method handle unseen speech styles or accents?

Incomplete inference analysis: Computational overhead of bypasses vs. baseline unclear. CFG disabled in Stage 2 unjustified. Batch size effects on guidance scaling unexamined. Potential γv-γa interactions unexplored

Ethical considerations absent: Portrait generation with identity+voice control raises deepfake concerns. No discussion of societal impact or misuse prevention despite clear practical applications in synthetic media

strengths: Addresses a well-motivated problem: unifying visual and acoustic control in joint audio-video generation, a genuine gap in existing methods

Comprehensive experimental evaluation with quantitative metrics (Sync-C/D, CLIP, DINO, depth/pose MAE), human evaluation (20 participants, 6 criteria), audio quality analysis, ablations, and concurrent work comparison
Practical working system demonstrating controllable joint audio-video generation with multiple control modalities (reference images, audio, depth, pose)
Modality-specific inference-time guidance scaling (γ_v, γ_a) is a useful feature enabling independent control without retraining
Efficient training (12 hours on 4 H200 GPUs) and clear presentation with good visualizations of results
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: MMCU is standard VAE encoding + mask concatenation; Dual-Stream Bypass directly applies ControlNet-style architecture; two-stage inference is inherited from LTX-2; guidance scaling is simple scalar multiplication. Primarily engineering combination of existing techniques, not fundamental algorithmic innovation

Critical baseline mismatch: SadTalker, AniPortrait, Hallo3 are visual-centric or audio-driven portrait methods, NOT joint audio-video systems. Comparison is unfair—baselines use ground-truth audio/frames while MMControl generates both, contradicting the claim that this disadvantage is addressed. Improvements vs. comparable methods are marginal (Text CLIP: 0.2546 vs. 0.2337; Subject DINO: 0.8948 vs. 0.8873)

Insufficient concurrent baselines: Only AVControl compared (Appendix D), and only on depth/pose, not audio. For 2025/2026 work claiming SOTA, more joint audio-video baselines essential. This limits ability to assess true advancement

Technical depth lacking: No justification for even-numbered bypass interleaving; ablation (B4) shows audio-video cross-attention helps, contradicting the 'intra-modality specialization' rationale. Missing mechanistic analysis (no attention visualizations, feature analysis, or explanation of audio-visual interaction during diffusion)

Experimental validation issues: Human evaluation on only 200 total samples (20 participants, 5 per method) lacks statistical power; no significance testing. Evaluation metrics are coarse (Text CLIP from 8 frames; Dynamic Degree via optical flow). Audio quality evaluated on only 150 samples. No domain diversity—all Hallo3 (portrait animation)

Reproducibility and generalization concerns: Heavy reliance on preprocessing tools (GroundedSAM-2, Depth-Anything-v2, DWPose, Qwen2.5-Omni) with no error propagation analysis; no stated code/model release. Training on only 30,000 samples (small by modern standards) from single domain. Entire system depends on LTX-2 backbone; generalization to other joint DiTs unclear

Limited scope: Single-character portrait animation only. Multi-character/conversational scenarios relegated to future work. Structured text format [VISUAL]/[SPEECH] required; flexibility unstated. Inference time not reported; cannot assess computational cost. No failure case analysis

Overstated claims: 'State-of-the-art' primarily vs. non-joint baselines (Table 1); vs. AVControl (Table S5) improvements modest. 'Fine-grained, composable control' not systematically evaluated (e.g., depth + audio + identity together). 'Preserves inherent cross-modal synchronization' lacks detailed analysis beyond Sync-C metric

Design choices lack justification: Mask concatenation (Eq. 4) appears arbitrary; no ablation testing alternative designs. Why bypass at even layers? Why omit modality cross-attention in branches (ablation contradicts stated reasoning). No comparison vs. simpler baselines (e.g., standard ControlNet + scalar scaling on LTX-2)

strengths: Well-motivated problem: Addresses genuine gap in unified multi-modal control for joint audio-video generation, which is timely and practically important

Comprehensive experimental evaluation: Multiple metrics (Sync-C/D, CLIP, DINO, MAE), comparisons with diverse baselines, human evaluation (20 raters, 3.58 vs 3.22 next-best), audio quality metrics, and detailed ablations

Strong empirical results: Achieves highest audio-visual sync despite baselines having GT audio advantage; best/competitive structural control (depth/pose MAE); consistent human evaluation wins across 6 criteria

Sound technical design: MMCU cleanly unifies heterogeneous inputs via masking; Dual-Stream Bypass preserves frozen priors while enabling modality-specific learning; Guidance Scaling provides elegant inference-time control

Clear presentation: Well-organized, helpful figures, comprehensive supplementary material with ablations and qualitative results
weaknesses: Limited algorithmic novelty: Components (MMCU masking, Dual-Stream Bypass, scalar guidance scaling) are straightforward adaptations of existing techniques (ControlNet, T2I-Adapter) to this context; contribution is primarily system integration rather than fundamental innovation

Inadequate comparison with joint audio-video baselines: Sora 2, Veo 3, JavisDiT, LTX-2, Universe mentioned but not compared quantitatively; baselines (SadTalker, AniPortrait) were not designed for joint generation, limiting insights into relative approach merits

Narrow scope and scalability concerns: Single-character, single-speaker only (acknowledged but unaddressed); unclear generalization from 30K curated Hallo3 samples; no results on multi-character dialogue or diverse speech styles; acoustic control limited to reference timbre via pre-recorded audio
